questions.question: Profit rose from ₹-15.33 crore in FY24 to ₹43.83 crore in FY26, but only 54.6% of operating profit came in as cash. What does that suggest?

choices.text: The business is doing brilliantly; cash doesn't matter.
Some profit may be stuck in unpaid bills or unsold goods, so check how fast customers pay.
The company must have paid a big dividend.
Profit and cash are always equal, so the figures must be wrong.

questions.explanation: Profit is counted when a sale is made; cash arrives when the customer pays. For Paras Healthcare Limited, only 54.6% of operating profit turned into cash, so money is getting stuck. Trade receivables and inventory are where to look.

questions.question: At the top price, Paras Healthcare Limited's P/E is 159.7x. Similar listed companies have a P/E of about 57.4x. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It costs about the same as, or less than, similar companies for each rupee of profit.
It costs more than similar companies for each rupee of profit, so its profit must grow faster to be worth it.
The P/E shows how many shares the company has.

questions.explanation: A P/E of 159.7x against 57.4x means you pay far more for each rupee of Paras Healthcare Limited's profit than for its peers'. Its profit would need to grow much faster for that to pay off.

questions.question: 65.5% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹500 crore here, reaches Paras Healthcare Limited.

questions.question: Sales went from ₹1,129.04 crore in FY24 to ₹1,605.95 crore in FY26, which is 19.3% a year. How would you describe that?
questions.explanation: 19.3% a year is healthy growth: Paras Healthcare Limited's customers are buying more each year.
